development_2024.interpretation: Under beta_sqrt>=0 and beta_error>=0, every candidate with a free slope was infeasible because at least one fitted slope was negative. The only feasible active set fixed both slopes to zero.

interpretation: The monotonicity constraints corrected the unsafe sign behavior found in the unconstrained controller.
But the 2024 data contained no positive monotone slope signal in either SQRT risk or competence-error feature.
The constrained optimum therefore collapsed to an intercept-only BAD risk of 16/42 = 38.10%.
Because 38.10% exceeds the frozen WATCH upper threshold of 35%, every 2025 SQRT alarm was retained.
This is maximally safe for true DOWN retention but provides zero false-alarm reduction.
The failure is not due to score drift; it shows that the chosen two-feature monotone logistic surface cannot justify suppression from 2024 evidence.
decision.next_step: Proceed to a separately preregistered Learn-Then-Test / risk-control action calibration, which can control action risk without requiring a parametric monotone probability surface to discover a stable slope.
